resources.string: Optional, off by default. Each switch lets a computer you linked and allowed on its side ask this phone for that data while the link is up. Switching it off stops sharing at once.
Share contacts
Read-only: names, numbers, emails for the Contacts app on your computer. Photos are never sent.
Share calendar
Read-only by default: events (with calendar, reminders and attendee names) from the calendars you tick, from 7 days back to 90 days ahead. Includes Google Calendar accounts that sync on this phone.
Let the computer edit my calendar
Lets a linked computer you allowed add, change and delete one-off events in the calendars you ticked (never repeating events). Android asks for calendar write access only when you switch this on.

GeekBridge never signs in to Google. Edits are written to this phone\'s calendar and Google Calendar receives them through the phone\'s own sync. Remove the permission here or in Android settings to stop it at any time.
Choose calendars…
No calendar ticked: nothing is shared yet
No calendars found on this phone.
Share text messages (SMS)
Lets the computer list your SMS conversations, show new ones, and send a text through this phone.
Share battery level

Sends only the charge percentage, whether the phone is charging and a low-battery flag to the computers you allow, while they are connected. No permission needed. The computer keeps it in memory only.
Show phone notifications on the computer

Shows notifications of the apps you pick on the computers you allow, and lets that computer dismiss them or press their buttons (never type a reply). Needs Notification access, which Android asks you to switch on in its own settings.
Show recent photos on the computer

When an allowed computer asks, shows it your newest photos as small previews. A full picture is sent only when you press Save or Copy on that computer. Nothing is uploaded in the background. Needs access to your photos, which Android asks you for.

Android 13+ greys out Notification access for apps installed outside a store. Open app settings, tap ⋮ (top right) › Allow restricted settings (on Samsung: Settings › Apps › GeekBridge › ⋮), confirm with your PIN, then open Notification access again and switch GeekBridge on.

Ongoing, call, secret and GeekBridge\'s own notifications and app icons are never sent. Only the title and text Android shows, the app name, the time and up to three buttons that need no typing are sent, only while the computer is linked and allowed, and only to the computers ticked above. Text is never logged here. The computer holds at most 50 per phone, in memory, for 3 hours; it shows a banner with the app name (and the text only if you turned that on there). Withdrawing the switch, the computer, the app or the access stops it at once.

Short codes and premium numbers
Off: the computer cannot text numbers shorter than 7 digits or premium-rate ranges. They can cost money.

Android restricts SMS: reading and sending needs the SMS permissions (read, send, receive), and Google Play only allows them for the default messaging app. This build asks for them only when you switch this on. On Android 13+, an app installed outside a store may first need “Allow restricted settings” in its App info (⋮ menu). GeekBridge does not become your default messaging app. Not supported: MMS pictures, group texts, RCS chats. Message text goes only to your linked computer and is never logged.

Android blocks SMS for apps installed outside a store (“restricted setting”). Missing: %1$s. Open app settings, tap ⋮ (top right) › Allow restricted settings, then Permissions › SMS › Allow. If ⋮ has no such item yet, tap “Allow access” once and look again.
SMS is allowed on this phone, but no computer is linked. Link a computer first.
SMS is allowed on this phone, but no linked computer may use it. Tap “Allowed computers…” and tick your computer.

This phone has two SIM slots. To let your computer choose which SIM sends a text, GeekBridge must be allowed to see your SIM cards (Android calls this “Phone” access, the same one the call features use). It is optional: without it every text is sent from your phone’s default SIM.
Choosing a SIM is off because Android will not ask again, so every text is sent from your phone’s default SIM. To change that, open app settings › Permissions › Phone and choose Allow.
